text:
ConocoPhillips rose modestly today as crude oil prices held firm in the $100–126 range, supported by ongoing geopolitical tension in the Middle East. Over the past week, attacks by Houthi militants on Saudi Arabian and shipping infrastructure have kept upward pressure on oil prices, and that broader market strength has lifted the stock along with it. The company also benefits from the wide gap between U.S. crude ($101.91/barrel) and global crude ($126.55/barrel), which creates pricing advantages for U.S. refiners and producers with export optionality.

The two-week rally of nearly 13% fits into a larger pattern where Middle East unrest has been a consistent tailwind for oil and energy stocks. While today's specific move was incremental, it reflects market participants pricing in a sustained period of tighter global oil supplies driven by regional instability.
